interface.title: GTsR — A GNN Based Tool for Solvent Removal from MOF with stability check (Xiao-Yan Li group 'MACE Tools' Streamlit app)
interface.stage_of_work: Structure curation before molecular simulation or high-throughput screening
interface.what_it_is_for: Upload a raw MOF crystal structure (CIF), have a graph neural network remove free and/or bound solvent molecules, look at the cleaned framework and the removed solvent (with SMILES), and download the cleaned CIF. An optional check of activation stability is offered, but it failed in this deployment.

data.note: I uploaded ABEXEM.cif (La MOF, C56H40La8N16O80, 200 atoms), then 7230226_R.cif (La MOF, C80H68La4N4O54, 210 atoms) and c6dt04596k2_3_R.cif (Zn MOF, C92H110N6O24Zn2, 234 atoms). The app has no built-in example data. Three cleaned CIFs were downloaded: ABEXEM_gtsr.cif twice (Free Only and All) and 7230226_R_gtsr.cif.

features.name: Crystal structure 3D viewer with style, label and spin controls
features.general: Show a periodic 3D structure in an embedded viewer with its unit cell and axes; switch the drawing style, toggle per-atom element labels and auto-spin; rotate and zoom with the mouse; show the formula and atom count beside it
features.specific: Raw Structure / Cleaned Structure panels: Style (Ball and stick / Stick / Space filling / Line), Element (Hide / Show), Rotation (Off / On), plus Chemical Formula and Number of Atoms, rendered with py3Dmol/stmol
steps: Upload a CIF so the viewer shows the unit cell
Choose a Style (Ball and stick, Stick, Space filling, Line)
Turn Element labels on or off
Turn Rotation on for a spinning view, or drag and use the wheel to rotate and zoom by hand
Read the Chemical Formula and Number of Atoms metrics
serves_tasks: Load a structure file and get its composition summary
Look at the 3D structure in different renderings
Look at the cleaned or removed parts in 3D with labels and motion

features.name: Model-based guest removal with mode and decision threshold
features.general: Run a classifier that decides which parts of a structure are removable guests. Choose a removal scope and a decision cutoff, then rerun to compare. A notice clears stale results when the input or the mode changes, but not when only the cutoff changes
features.specific: Solvent Type (Free Only vs All) + threshold number input (step 0.1, max 1.00) + 'Start Cleaning Your MOF'. Changing the CIF or the Solvent Type clears the previous result and shows 'The target was changed, please re-predict for it.' Changing only the threshold does not clear or flag the previous result: it stays on screen under the new threshold until you rerun (screens/043.webp shows the old H24O32 result under 1.00)
steps: Pick Solvent Type: Free Only (unbound guests) or All (also metal-bound guests)
Set the threshold by typing or with the −/+ steppers (step 0.1; if + is disabled short of 1.00, e.g. at 0.95, type the value)
Press Start Cleaning Your MOF; after a threshold-only change, always rerun, since the old result is not cleared
Read the new formula and atom count; change the mode or threshold and rerun to compare
serves_tasks: Remove both unbound and metal-bound guest molecules
Change the model's decision cutoff and rerun to see how much is removed

features.name: Kept/removed split view with fragment SMILES list
features.general: After splitting a structure into a kept part and a removed part, switch one viewer between the two. Each part shows its own formula and atom count, and the removed fragments are listed as distinct chemical identifiers
features.specific: The Content selector (Framework / Solvent) in Cleaned Structure, with the 'Solvents N: <SMILES>' info boxes under the viewer when Solvent is chosen
steps: Choose Content 'Framework' to see the cleaned framework and its formula
Choose Content 'Solvent' to see only the removed molecules in the same cell
Read the unique solvent SMILES (e.g. CN(C)C=O for DMF, O for water, [O] for an O atom with no H in the CIF)
serves_tasks: Compare the removed fragments against the cleaned structure

features.name: Processed-structure export
features.general: Download the processed structure as a standard file named after the input, ready for the next tool
features.specific: The 'Download Cleaned MOF' button saves <input>_gtsr.cif, a P1 CIF written by pymatgen. It always holds the framework, whichever Content is being viewed
steps: Run cleaning in the chosen mode
Use the downloaded <name>_gtsr.cif in simulation or screening

screens_never_reached: Activation Stability Prediction result: 'Want to check stability?' always failed with 'FileNotFoundError: Zeo++ executable 'network' was not found in PATH' (screens/030.webp, screens/056.webp), so no stability score or verdict was ever shown
The 'Your structure without any solvent.' message for a structure where the model finds nothing to remove (named by the reviewer from the code; no tested file triggered it)
not_done: Check whether the cleaned framework is predicted to be stable after activation (Activation Stability Prediction > 'Want to check stability?'), a core stage per the page subtitle 'with stability check': blocked on the server side because the Zeo++ 'network' binary needed for pore-diameter features is missing. Tried on ABEXEM (Free Only, screens/030.webp) and on 7230226_R (All, screens/056.webp); both crashed with FileNotFoundError, so it is kept out of the tree.
Thresholds below 0.50 were not tried. Only 0.50, 0.90 and 1.00 were run, and only on ABEXEM.
The 'All' mode and the Solvent/SMILES view were not run on the third file (c6dt04596k2_3_R.cif). Only Free Only at 0.50 was run on it.
The case where the model finds no solvent to remove was not reached.
In the original run the drag on the 3D viewer happened during a re-render, so manual rotation was not seen there; the replay did see dragging rotate the cell. Wheel zoom visibly worked in both.
